summary: John H. Berthrong (1946–2022) worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu around 1974–1979 and held a post at Boston University from circa 1989 to 2013.

John Henry Wright (1852–1908) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1869–1873) and held academic posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1886–1887) and Harvard University (~1887–1908).
John Herbert Harington (1765–1828) worked in indology and history and archaeology. He served as secretary of the Asiatic Society and was a professor at Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1808.

John J. Holder is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and served at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1990) and has held posts at Boston College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

John Jorgensen specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner (1979) and held appointments at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2003–2011) and was appointed Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University around 2011.
John Lockwood Kipling (1837–1911) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum from circa 1875 to 1893.

John M. Koller works in philosophy, religious studies, and indology. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles A. Moore, and served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (attested 1988–1999).

John M. Rosenfield (1924–2013) worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Southern Methodist University, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University, where he served as professor from circa 1960 to 1991.

John Marshall (1876–1958) was an indologist and archaeologist who studied at Dulwich College, King's College, and the University of Cambridge. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.
John Marston is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997 and held a post at El Colegio de México.

John Muir (1810–1882) was an indologist educated at East India Company College and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), founded the University of Edinburgh, and held a post there (~1862–1882).
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (~1968–1987) and Namkhai Norbu.

John Nemec is an indologist and scholar of religion and philosophy. Educated at Rochester, UC Santa Barbara, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005), he studied under Alexis Sanderson and became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020).
John Okell (1934–2020) was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College (~1953–1957). He held an academic post at SOAS University of London from circa 1965 to 1999.

John P. Keenan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, was a research fellow at Nanzan Institute (1983–1986), and taught at Middlebury College (attested 1989, 2006).

John Peile (1837–1910) was a scholar of linguistics and indology. He was educated at St. Bees School, Repton School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, and studied under Theodor Benfey from circa 1866 to 1869.
John Pickford was an indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia (~1985–1991). He held positions at the Australian National University (~1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and the University of Melbourne (2022).
